newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel buries schoolgirls killed by Jordanian.
newsitem.headline: Israel buries schoolgirls killed by Jordanian.

text.p: Mothers' screams tore through the night air on Thursday as thousands of mourners buried four of the seven girls shot dead by a Jordanian soldier during a school trip to a usually peaceful border.
The funeral in Beit Shemesh and burials of the three other victims in nearby communities were held in accordance with Orthodox Jewish tradition as soon as possible after their deaths.
The girls, eighth-graders aged 13 and 14, attended a religious school in Beit Shemesh, a working-class town near Jerusalem.

"They were murdered because of one thing -- because they are daughters of the people of Israel and because of a great and terrible hatred aimed at ending our existence here," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a eulogy.

"If anyone thinks the murder of little girls will bring this people to its knees...break our spirit or that we will relinquish our birthright, holy land and our eternal capital, he does not know the strength that exists in each person standing here around me today and in the entire nation," he said.
Netanyahu's remarks were a clear reference to recent Arab-Israeli tensions over his right-wing government's plan to build 6,500 more homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.
Jordan's King Hussein said in a letter to Netanyahu released this week that the policy could lead to bloodshed.
"I want her back," the mother of one of the girls shouted as Netanyahu spoke.

But there were no shouted calls for revenge or chants of "Death to the Arabs" heard at many past funerals of Jews killed by Arabs. Unlike the peace deal with the Palestinians, Israel's 1994 treaty with Jordan was widely welcomed in the Jewish state.
Lightning flashed as four burial shrouds were lowered into their graves. Some relatives fainted and mourners cried out as Netanyahu and other dignitaries read out the girls' names.
"All the buses that left Beit Shemesh were full of the joy of life. They came back filled with despair and mourning," Education Minister Zvulun Hammer said at the funeral.
"It was not a school trip, it was the final path.
"How much longer must we go to funerals of small children who were taken from us when they were only young flowers?" Hammer said. "The River Jordan is now red with their innocent blood."
